ei.title: Why Fashion Needs to Be More Sustainable
ei.subject: 공통영어1

fullPassage:
Why Fashion Needs to Be More Sustainable

Jessi is a fashion blogger who loves unique, vibrant clothes. But guess what? She does not buy new clothes. Instead, she buys them secondhand. You may think secondhand clothes are old-fashioned, but by buying them, Jessi can try different styles. She also does not get too attached to any style or brand because there is always another exciting outfit waiting to be discovered. Jessi's clothing habits are not just about creating a style; they are about saving the Earth. The reason is that her actions help reduce the production and consumption of clothes.

Worth over $3 trillion and making up 2% of the world's GDP, the fashion industry today has an almost entirely linear approach. The process moves in a straight line from design to consumption to disposal. Material extraction, textile manufacturing, the supply chain, design, sales, marketing, and other steps are guided by the aim of maximizing garment consumption without considering other issues. Due to linear fashion, the fashion industry negatively affects the environment. 85% of textiles go into landfills, only 1% of the materials is recycled, at least 500,000 tons of microfibers end up in the ocean (equal to 50 billion plastic bottles), and 93 billion cubic meters of water is required for textile production annually. Alarming numbers like these will keep increasing if producers maintain the old system. It is clear that waste and pollution from the fashion industry must be reduced. Linear fashion must change, and this could happen through circular fashion.

Circular fashion is inspired by the principles of a circular economy and sustainable development. A circular economy is based on limiting waste, keeping resources and materials in use, and reusing them. In a circular model, we make, use, and reuse materials for as long as possible to extract their maximum value. Therefore, clothing and textiles are produced, used, and reused to minimize waste. It is a renewable approach to reduce the fashion industry's environmental impact. Circular fashion provides numerous benefits. First, extending the lifespan of fibers significantly reduces textile waste, benefiting the environment. Second, circular processes utilize chemicals and materials safe for human health and the environment. This practice protects the environment and consumer health. Third, materials are regenerated instead of being disposed of, which enables their long-term use.

The rise of circular fashion is facilitated by new technology and ideas. Materials commonly used in clothing are not eco-friendly because they require considerable resources and often break down slowly. This creates a need for eco-friendly textile alternatives. Currently, companies are developing recycled fibers and fibers extracted from agricultural waste products like leaves, peels, and seeds. One company uses nanotechnology to make soft material from orange peels. Another makes fabrics from kapok tree seeds. The trees grow well in poor soil without needing much water. These new fabrics produce less waste, last a long time, and break down easily.

In addition to these manufacturing techniques, technology will improve in such a way that it may become normal to produce clothes only when people order them. This "make-to-order" method will cost more, but then less money will be spent on maintaining offline stores. And 3D technology will enable people to see how clothes will fit online without trying them on in a store. In the long run, innovation in production and sales will facilitate sustainable fashion and considerably reduce material waste and logistics emissions.

Another key to making fashion sustainable is the consumer: us. If we want the fashion industry to adopt more sustainable practices, we must care about how clothes come to us. We should then demonstrate our concerns through what we buy. The market, of course, will respond. We can also reduce waste by discarding clothes responsibly. To be specific, we should buy only what we need and pass clothing on to someone who will wear it or to a thrift shop when discarding it.

Circular fashion will not solve every problem in the fashion industry overnight. However, small steps in the right direction are better than nothing. Keeping things in the supply chain for as many cycles as possible is really important. By making small changes to our clothing habits today, the fashion industry will gradually improve. After all, nothing is more fashionable than saving the planet.

questions.passage: Another key to making fashion sustainable is the consumer: us.  If we want the fashion industry ①<u>to adopt</u> more sustainable practices, we must care about how clothes come to us.  We should then demonstrate our concerns through ②<u>that</u> we buy.  The market, of course, will respond.  We can also reduce waste by ③<u>discarding</u> clothes responsibly.  To be specific, we should buy only what we need and pass clothing on to someone who will ④<u>wear</u> it or to a thrift shop when discarding it.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① to adopt(채택하다) → 정상 / ② that → what(~하는 것) / ③ discarding(버리는 것) → 정상 / ④ wear(입다) → 정상.
det.analysis:
✅ ① to adopt: want + O + to V — 정상.
❌ ② that: 원문은 what. 'through what we buy'에서 what은 선행사 포함 관계대명사(= the things that). that은 전치사 through 뒤에서 이 역할 불가. ←정답
✅ ③ discarding: 전치사 by 뒤 동명사 — 정상.
✅ ④ wear: someone who will wear — 관계대명사절 내 동사원형 정상.
det.tip: what = the thing(s) that. 선행사 포함 관계대명사.

The process moves in a straight line from design to consumption to disposal. Due to linear fashion, the fashion industry negatively affects the environment.  85% of textiles ②<u>go</u> into landfills, only 1% of the materials is recycled, at least 500,000 tons of microfibers end up in the ocean (equal to 50 billion plastic bottles), and 93 billion cubic meters of water is required for textile production annually.  Alarming numbers like these will ③<u>keep</u> increasing if producers ④<u>maintains</u> the old system.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① are guided(이끌리다) → 정상 / ② go(가다) → 정상 / ③ keep(계속하다) → 정상 / ④ maintains → maintain(유지하다).
det.analysis:
✅ ① are guided: 수동태 정상 (steps are guided by).
✅ ② go: 85% of textiles go — 복수 주어 + 복수 동사 정상.
✅ ③ keep: will keep increasing — 조동사 will 뒤 동사원형 정상.
❌ ④ maintains: 원문은 maintain. 주어 producers(복수)이므로 동사원형 maintain 필요. maintains(3인칭 단수)는 틀림. ←정답
det.tip: 주어 producers(복수) → 동사원형 maintain. maintains는 단수 주어용.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① extending(연장하는 것) → 정상 / ② being disposed(폐기되는 것) → 정상 / ③ that → which(계속적 용법) / ④ slowly(느리게) → 정상.
det.analysis:
✅ ① extending: 동명사 주어 — 정상.
✅ ② being disposed: instead of being disposed of — 전치사 뒤 동명사 수동형 정상.
❌ ③ that: 원문은 which. 콤마 뒤 계속적 용법의 관계대명사는 which만 가능. that은 계속적 용법(, that)에 쓸 수 없음. ←정답
✅ ④ slowly: break down slowly — 부사 정상.
det.tip: 계속적 용법(콤마 + 관계대명사): which만 가능. that 불가.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 제한하는. 극대화하다. 이롭게 하는. 안전한.
det.analysis:
✅ ① limiting: limiting waste — 폐기물을 제한. 원문 그대로.
❌ ② maximize: 원문은 minimize. 순환 모델에서 폐기물을 '최소화'해야 문맥에 맞음. maximize(극대화)는 문맥 반대. ←정답
✅ ③ benefiting: benefiting the environment — 원문 그대로.
✅ ④ safe: materials safe for human health — 원문 그대로.
det.tip: minimize(최소화) ↔ maximize(극대화). 순환 패션 목적 = 폐기물 최소화.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 촉진하다. 줄이다. 무시하다. 줄이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① facilitate: facilitate sustainable fashion — 원문 그대로.
✅ ② reduce: considerably reduce — 원문 그대로.
❌ ③ ignore: 원문은 care about. 지속가능한 관행을 위해 옷이 오는 과정에 '관심을 가져야 한다(care about)'. ignore(무시하다)는 문맥 반대. ←정답
✅ ④ reduce: reduce waste — 원문 그대로.
det.tip: care about(관심을 갖다) ↔ ignore(무시하다).

questions.passage: Jessi is a fashion blogger who loves unique, vibrant clothes.  But guess what?  She does not buy new clothes.  Instead, she buys them secondhand.  You may think secondhand clothes are old-fashioned, but by buying them, Jessi can try different styles.  She also does not get too ______ to any style or brand because there is always another exciting outfit waiting to be discovered.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 어떤 스타일에도 지나치게 ~하지 않는다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① attached(애착을 가진): 원문 그대로. get too attached to = ~에 지나치게 애착을 갖다. 항상 새 옷을 발견할 수 있으므로 애착하지 않는다는 문맥에 부합. ←정답
❌ ② accustomed(익숙해진): get accustomed to는 '~에 익숙해지다'로 의미가 다름. 스타일에 익숙해지는 것과 애착은 다른 개념.
❌ ③ resistant(저항하는): get resistant to는 '~에 저항하는'으로 문맥과 안 맞음.
❌ ④ related(관련된): get related to는 비표준적 표현이며 문맥 부적합.
det.tip: get attached to = ~에 애착을 갖다.

questions.passage: Circular fashion will not solve every problem in the fashion industry overnight.  However, small steps in the right direction are better than nothing.  Keeping things in the supply chain for as many cycles as possible is really important.  By making small changes to our clothing habits today, the fashion industry will ______ improve.  After all, nothing is more fashionable than saving the planet.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 점진적으로 개선될 것이다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① immediately(즉시): 앞 문장에서 '하루아침에 해결 못 한다(not overnight)'고 했으므로 즉시 개선은 문맥 모순.
❌ ② accidentally(우연히): 작은 변화를 '의도적으로' 주는 것이므로 우연히는 문맥 부적합.
❌ ③ temporarily(일시적으로): 지속적인 개선이 필요하다는 문맥에 일시적은 반대.
✅ ④ gradually(점진적으로): 원문 그대로. 작은 변화 → 점진적 개선이라는 문맥에 부합. ←정답
det.tip: gradually = 점진적으로. not overnight → small steps → gradually.

questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: ① 스타일+지구. ② 새 옷 구매. ③ 중고=구식. ④ 브랜드 애착.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 제시의 옷 습관은 스타일뿐 아니라 지구를 구하기 위한 것이다. — not just about creating a style; they are about saving the Earth. 원문 일치. ←정답
❌ ② 제시는 새 옷을 사서 스타일을 시도한다. — She does not buy new clothes. 새 옷을 사지 않으므로 불일치.
❌ ③ 제시는 중고 옷이 구식이라고 생각한다. — You may think (독자가 생각할 수 있다), 제시가 그렇게 생각한다는 내용 아님.
❌ ④ 제시는 특정 브랜드에 강한 애착을 보인다. — does not get too attached. 불일치.
det.tip: not just about A; about B = A뿐만 아니라 B이기도 하다.

ch: 제시의 옷 습관은 스타일뿐 아니라 지구를 구하기 위한 것이다.
제시는 새 옷을 사서 다양한 스타일을 시도한다.
제시는 특정 브랜드에 강한 애착을 보인다.

questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: ① 폐기물 제한 기반. ② 최대 가치 추출. ③ 안전한 화학물질. ④ 재료 폐기.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 순환 경제는 폐기물 제한과 자원 재사용에 기반한다. — based on limiting waste... and reusing them. 원문 일치.
❌ ② 순환 모델에서는 재료의 최대 가치를 추출하기 위해 오래 사용한다. — for as long as possible to extract their maximum value. 원문 일치.
❌ ③ 순환 과정은 인간 건강에 안전한 화학 물질을 이용한다. — materials safe for human health. 원문 일치.
✅ ④ 순환 패션에서 재료는 재생되지 않고 폐기된다. — regenerated instead of being disposed of. 재생된다고 했으므로 '폐기된다'는 불일치. ←정답
det.tip: regenerated ≠ disposed of. 순환 패션은 재생(regenerated)을 지향.

ch: 순환 경제는 폐기물 제한과 자원 재사용에 기반한다.
순환 모델에서는 재료의 최대 가치를 추출하기 위해 오래 사용한다.
순환 과정은 인간 건강에 안전한 화학 물질을 이용한다.
순환 패션에서 재료는 재생되지 않고 폐기된다.

questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: ① 친환경적. ② 나노기술=카폭. ③ 비옥+물. ④ 폐기물↓+분해↑.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 의류에 흔히 사용되는 재료는 친환경적이다. — not eco-friendly. 불일치.
❌ ② 한 회사는 카폭 나무 씨앗에서 나노기술을 개발한다. — 나노기술은 오렌지 껍질 회사(One company uses nanotechnology... orange peels). 카폭은 다른 회사(Another makes fabrics from kapok). 불일치.
❌ ③ 카폭 나무는 비옥한 토양과 많은 물이 필요하다. — poor soil without needing much water. 불일치.
✅ ④ 새로운 직물들은 폐기물을 덜 생산하고 쉽게 분해된다. — produce less waste... break down easily. 원문 일치. ←정답
det.tip: produce less waste + break down easily = 친환경 신소재의 장점.

ch: 한 회사는 카폭 나무 씨앗에서 나노기술을 개발한다.
카폭 나무는 비옥한 토양과 많은 물이 필요하다.
새로운 직물들은 폐기물을 덜 생산하고 쉽게 분해된다.

questions.passage:
Another key to making fashion sustainable is the consumer: us.  If we want the fashion industry to adopt more sustainable practices, we must care about how clothes come to us.  We should then demonstrate our concerns through what we buy.  The market, of course, will respond.  We can also reduce waste by discarding clothes responsibly.  To be specific, we should buy only what we need and pass clothing on to someone who will wear it or to a thrift shop when discarding it.

Circular fashion will not solve every problem in the fashion industry overnight.  However, small steps in the right direction are better than nothing.  Keeping things in the supply chain for as many cycles as possible is really important.  By making small changes to our clothing habits today, the fashion industry will gradually improve.  After all, nothing is more fashionable than saving the planet.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 소비자의 의식적 소비+폐기가 패션 산업 변화의 핵심.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 패션 기업은 소비자 요구를 무시하고 독자적으로 변화해야 한다. — The market will respond. 시장은 반응한다고 했으므로 무시와 반대.
❌ ② 순환 패션은 모든 문제를 즉시 해결할 수 있는 완벽한 해법이다. — will not solve every problem overnight. 즉시 해결 불가.
✅ ③ 지속 가능한 패션을 위해 소비자가 구매와 폐기 습관을 바꿔야 한다. ←정답: demonstrate concerns through what we buy + discarding responsibly.
❌ ④ 패션 산업의 변화는 기술 혁신에만 달려 있고 소비자 역할은 미미하다. — Another key is the consumer: us. 소비자가 핵심이라고 강조.
det.tip: 요지 = 소비자가 구매와 폐기를 통해 지속 가능한 패션에 기여.

ch: 패션 기업은 소비자 요구를 무시하고 독자적으로 변화해야 한다.
순환 패션은 모든 문제를 즉시 해결할 수 있는 완벽한 해법이다.
지속 가능한 패션을 위해 소비자가 구매와 폐기 습관을 바꿔야 한다.
패션 산업의 변화는 기술 혁신에만 달려 있고 소비자 역할은 미미하다.

questions.passage: Circular fashion will not solve every problem in the fashion industry overnight.  However, small steps in the right direction are better than nothing.  Keeping things in the supply chain for as many cycles as possible is really important.  By making small changes to our clothing habits today, the fashion industry will gradually improve.  After all, nothing is more <u>fashionable</u> than saving the planet.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 fashionable이 이 문맥에서 함축하는 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: fashionable = 유행을 따르는 → 문맥에서는 '가장 가치 있고 바람직한'.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 값비싼 — 비용과 무관한 문맥.
❌ ② 유행을 따르는 — 글자 그대로의 의미. 여기서는 패션(유행)과 환경 보호를 연결한 비유적 표현.
✅ ③ 가치 있고 바람직한 ←정답: 지구를 구하는 것이 가장 '유행에 맞는(가치 있는)' 일이라는 비유. 패션의 본질을 환경 보호로 재정의.
❌ ④ 화려하고 눈에 띄는 — 외형적 특성이 아닌 가치 판단의 문맥.
det.tip: nothing is more fashionable than saving the planet = 지구를 구하는 것보다 더 가치 있는(세련된) 것은 없다.

questions.passage: Jessi is a fashion blogger who loves unique, vibrant clothes.  But guess what?  She does not buy new clothes.  Instead, she buys them secondhand.  You may think secondhand clothes are old-fashioned, but by buying <u>them</u>, Jessi can try different styles.  She also does not get too attached to any style or brand because there is always another exciting outfit waiting to be discovered.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 them이 가리키는 것은?

det.korean: 중고 옷. secondhand clothes를 대명사로 받음.
det.analysis:
앞 문장: secondhand clothes are old-fashioned, but by buying them → them = secondhand clothes(중고 옷).
❌ ① 새 옷 — She does not buy new clothes. 새 옷은 사지 않으므로 buying의 대상 아님.
✅ ② 중고 옷 ←정답: 직전 문맥의 secondhand clothes를 받음.
❌ ③ 패션 블로거들 — 복수형이지만 사람을 지칭하는 문맥 아님.
❌ ④ 다양한 스타일 — try different styles는 결과이지 buying의 대상 아님.
det.tip: them = secondhand clothes (직전 명사구를 받는 대명사).

questions.passage: Circular fashion is inspired by the principles of a circular economy and sustainable development.  A circular economy is based on limiting waste, keeping resources and materials in use, and reusing them.  In a circular model, we make, use, and reuse materials for as long as possible to extract <u>their</u> maximum value.  Therefore, clothing and textiles are produced, used, and reused to minimize waste.  It is a renewable approach to reduce the fashion industry's environmental impact.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 their가 가리키는 것은?

det.korean: 재료의. materials를 소유격 대명사로 받음.
det.analysis:
we make, use, and reuse materials for as long as possible to extract their maximum value → their = materials(재료).
❌ ① 순환 모델의 — 문법적으로 model's이 아닌 materials를 받음.
✅ ② 재료의 ←정답: materials를 make, use, reuse 하여 their(= materials의) maximum value를 추출.
❌ ③ 소비자의 — 소비자(we)는 주어이고 their는 목적어 materials를 받음.
❌ ④ 패션 산업의 — 패션 산업은 이 문장에 언급 안 됨.
det.tip: their = materials. 목적어를 소유격 대명사로 받음.

questions.passage: Circular fashion is inspired by the principles of a circular economy and sustainable development.  A circular economy is based on limiting waste, keeping resources and materials in use, and reusing them.  In a circular model, we make, use, and reuse materials for as long as possible to extract their maximum value.  Therefore, clothing and textiles are produced, used, and reused to minimize waste.  It is a renewable approach to reduce the fashion industry's environmental impact.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 순환 경제가 기반으로 하는 세 가지 원칙 중, '폐기물을 제한하는 것'에 해당하는 영어 표현을 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (2단어, 영어로)

det.korean: 폐기물을 제한하는 것.
det.analysis: A circular economy is based on limiting waste, keeping resources..., and reusing them. → 세 가지 원칙 중 첫 번째 = limiting waste. 찾기 유형이므로 passage 노출 정상.
det.tip: limiting waste = 폐기물을 제한하는 것.

questions.passage: The rise of circular fashion is facilitated by new technology and ideas.  Materials commonly used in clothing are not eco-friendly because they require considerable resources and often break down slowly.  This creates a need for eco-friendly textile alternatives.  Currently, companies are developing recycled fibers and fibers extracted from agricultural waste products like leaves, peels, and seeds.  One company uses nanotechnology to make soft material from orange peels.  Another makes fabrics from kapok tree seeds.  The trees grow well in poor soil without needing much water.  These new fabrics produce less waste, last a long time, and break down easily.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 의류에 흔히 사용되는 재료가 친환경적이지 않은 이유를 하나 본문에서 찾아 영어로 쓰시오. (3단어, 영어로)

det.korean: 느리게 분해된다. 친환경적이지 않은 이유 중 하나.
det.analysis: not eco-friendly because they require considerable resources and often break down slowly. → 이유 중 하나: break down slowly. 찾기 유형이므로 passage 노출 정상.
det.tip: break down slowly = 느리게 분해되다.

questions.passage:
The trees grow well in poor soil without needing much water.  These new fabrics produce less waste, last a long time, and break down easily.

In addition to these manufacturing techniques, technology will improve in such a way that it may become normal to produce clothes only when people order them.  This "make-to-order" method will cost more, but then less money will be spent on maintaining offline stores.  And 3D technology will enable people to see how clothes will fit online without trying them on in a store.  In the long run, innovation in production and sales will facilitate sustainable fashion and considerably reduce material waste and logistics emissions.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 생산과 판매의 혁신이 촉진하는 것을 나타내는 영어 표현을 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (2단어, 영어로)

det.korean: 지속 가능한 패션.
det.analysis: innovation in production and sales will facilitate sustainable fashion → 혁신이 촉진하는 것 = sustainable fashion. 찾기 유형이므로 passage 노출 정상.
det.tip: sustainable fashion = 지속 가능한 패션. facilitate = 촉진하다.

questions.passage: Circular fashion will not solve every problem in the fashion industry overnight.  However, small steps in the right direction are better than nothing.  Keeping things in the supply chain for as many cycles as possible is really important.  By making small changes to our clothing habits today, the fashion industry will gradually improve.  After all, nothing is more fashionable than ______.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 조건에 따라 영작하시오. (영어로)
"지구를 구하는 것"
[조건] (1) planet, saving, the를 모두 사용할 것
(2) 정확히 3단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: 지구를 구하는 것.
det.analysis: nothing is more fashionable than saving the planet. → 빈칸 = saving the planet (3단어).
det.tip: saving the planet = 지구를 구하는 것.

questions.passage: Circular fashion is inspired by the principles of a circular economy and sustainable development.  A circular economy is based on limiting waste, keeping resources and materials in use, and reusing them.  In a circular model, we make, use, and reuse materials for as long as possible to ______.  Therefore, clothing and textiles are produced, used, and reused to minimize waste.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 조건에 따라 영작하시오. (영어로)
"재료의 최대 가치를 추출하다"
[조건] (1) extract, maximum, their, value를 모두 사용할 것
(2) 정확히 4단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: 재료의 최대 가치를 추출하다.
det.analysis: reuse materials for as long as possible to extract their maximum value. → 빈칸 = extract their maximum value (4단어).
det.tip: extract their maximum value = 재료의 최대 가치를 추출하다. their = materials의.
